sections.heading: C — Yielding and traffic priority
sections.markdown:
## C — Yielding and traffic priority

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
At an uncontrolled meeting of vehicles or pedestrians, right-of-way rules identify who yields and who waits. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
The law assigns a duty to yield rather than granting an absolute right to proceed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
A driver must take every possible action to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle regardless of the situation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Yield to a pedestrian even when that pedestrian disobeys a traffic control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
When crossing a sidewalk to enter or leave a driveway, alley or parking lot, yield to pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Driving along a sidewalk is prohibited; crossing it is the permitted exception. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes the White Cane Law as protecting access to roads and sidewalks for people who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise physically disabled. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
The handbook cites the White Cane Law as 28-7-1 NMSA (1978). [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
Take all necessary injury-prevention precautions when approaching a blind or partially blind pedestrian using a predominantly white or metallic cane, with or without a red tip, or a guide dog. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
A driver who fails to take necessary injury-prevention precautions for a blind or partially blind pedestrian using a predominantly white or metallic cane, with or without a red tip, or a guide dog is liable for resulting injury damages. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
A left-turning driver yields to oncoming vehicles continuing straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
Before entering a traffic circle or rotary, yield to vehicles already circulating. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
At an intersection lacking a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal, give priority to vehicles approaching from the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first after making a complete stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
When vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right goes first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A01
A driver joining a road from a driveway, alley or roadside yields to vehicles on the main road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A01
Wait outside an intersection until the space beyond lets you cross it without stopping inside. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

Misconceptions: priority never removes the obligation to avoid a collision.
Mnemonics: entering waits for traffic already there.
Glossary: yielding means allowing another road user to proceed; a rotary is a traffic circle.
Dynamic facts: active emergency warnings, school-bus lights and the road divider determine the applicable response.

sections.heading: C2 — Yielding and traffic priority
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Yielding and traffic priority

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A02
A driver overtaking another vehicle moving in the same direction must yield to that vehicle even when it slows or stops. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A02
Yield to an emergency vehicle operating a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A02
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, pull to the right edge or as close to the right as possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A02
Follow instructions broadcast through an emergency vehicle’s loudspeaker. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside an intersection, clear the intersection before pulling over. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
Stop for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights whether it is beside your direction, opposite your direction or at the intersection you approach, except for the divided-road exception. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
You need not stop for an oncoming school bus when a median or other physical barrier separates the two directions of travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A02
After school-bus red lights stop flashing, remain stopped until children are completely off the roadway and proceeding is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A02
Yield to a train crossing the roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A02
If the state makes a public road one-way, it must post signs identifying that direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A02
On a signed one-way road, drive only in the indicated direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A02
When circulating around a traffic island, keep to the island’s right side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0015]
